No vowels ⁧درس⁩ , ⁧قبل⁩ , ⁧حضر⁩ may be I or II: decide the context (subject, complements). The form III instead is seen without vowels, because it has the ⁧ا⁩ after the first letter: ⁧قابل⁩ , ⁧شارك⁩ , ⁧ساعد⁩ .

The Arabic passive is made by changing the vowels of the verb; the subject of the action is usually not said. Without vowels the passive often has the same graph of the active: it is the context that reveals it (no action).

blocks.text: The pattern. Perfect: u on the first consonant, i on the penultimate ( ⁧كُتِبَ⁩ , ⁧قُدِّمَ⁩ , ⁧نُوقِشَ⁩ : ā of III becomes ū). Imperfect: u on the prefix, a on the penultimate ( ⁧يُكْتَبُ⁩ , ⁧يُقَدَّمُ⁩ , ⁧يُنَاقَشُ⁩ ). Useful phrases. ⁧وُلِدْتُ فِي مِيلَانُو⁩ I was born in Milan. ⁧يُقَالُ إِنَّ⁩ ... ... . ... it is said that... ⁧قِيلَ لِي⁩ I have been told that it is not. ⁧سُرِقَتْ سَيَّارَتُهُ⁩ They stole his car. ⁧يُمْنَعُ التَّدْخِينُ⁩ Smoking is prohibited (in notices); ⁧يُرْجَى⁩ Please ... ... ... ... ...A2-06). Agent's complement. When you want to say "from whom," in the journalistic style you use ⁧مِنْ قِبَلِ: نُوقِشَ القَانُونُ مِنْ قِبَلِ البَرْلَمَانِ⁩ The law was discussed by the parliament. But often you prefer the asset or ⁧تَمَّ⁩ + maṣdar (A2-16).

The double of form II. darrasa / darasa, ʿallama / ʿalima: The double is the only difference. You really keep it... The ā of form III. šāraka, qābala: ā is long and accented (šā-ra-ka). In the imperfect: yu-šā-ri-ku. The passive. kutiba, qīla, wulida, yuqālu: used to u-i (perfect) and u-a (perfect).
